summary: CLI exposes host to remote shell, file, and SSH command execution driven by vendor WebSocket/AppSync channel
details: @ai-support-agent/cli ships a `start` subcommand that connects to a vendor WebSocket and an AWS AppSync notification channel and treats the remote endpoint as a controller for the operator's host. `dist/commands/shell-executor.js` spawns `/bin/sh -c <payload.command>` where the payload is fetched via `client.getCommand` after an `AGENT_COMMAND` AppSync notification. `dist/commands/terminal-ws` decodes base64 bytes from remote WebSocket messages and writes them into a local `node-pty` session, giving the remote side an interactive PTY. `dist/commands/agent-transport.js`'s `processCommand`/`executeCommand` dispatcher additionally routes remote-delivered commands into `ssh-executor.js`, `file-executor.js`, and `process-executor.js`, adding arbitrary file read/write, process kill, and SSH-pivot execution using vendor-supplied credentials. The `dist/vscode/vscode-server.js` and `dist/browser/browser-local-server.js` components use `child_process` and local HTTP/ping surfaces to integrate this control channel with editor and browser hosts. Whoever controls the vendor endpoint — or gains any control over it — has full-host RCE, file, and SSH-pivot control over any machine running the CLI. The behavior only activates when the operator explicitly runs the CLI with a tenant token (not on `npm install` or on `require()`), but once running the remote-control surface is unconditional.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
